profile.summary: Apoorv Gogar is an accounting researcher who uses archival data to study how a firm's financial reporting affects the people who rely on it: creditors, information intermediaries such as credit rating agencies, and institutional investors. A central interest is how private lenders such as banks shape, and respond to, borrowers' reporting and disclosure. His working papers look at whether quarterly reporting lowers the cost of bank loans, what happened to Indian rating agencies and their clients after the ILFS default, and how fund-family conflicts shape index funds' securities lending.

themes.name: Financial reporting and bank debt
themes.description: Whether more frequent public reporting makes borrowers' private information more credible to lenders, and how that shows up in loan spreads and terms.

themes.name: Credit rating agencies and reputation
themes.description: The costs to rating agencies, and to the firms they rate, when an agency's reputation is damaged, studied through India's ILFS default.

themes.name: Institutional investors and conflicts of interest
themes.description: How fund-family interests influence passive funds' decisions to lend shares to short sellers.
